impl.summary: DBS D4 separation evaluation is built and was measured for real on this host's CPU ComfyUI through a running Fuobe (30 jobs across 2 runs). DBS-TIGER beats DBS-BSRNN on every mix (dialogue +1.2 to +2.1 dB SI-SDR) but is 2.4x slower here (0.10x vs 0.25x real time), so BSRNN stays the CPU default. The fast stereo bed (mono split) holds for centred dialogue (stereo gap 0.03-0.04, level within 0.6 dB) but fails for dialogue panned off-centre (bed SI-SDR 1 dB against 11 dB with each channel), so mono stays the default. On these synthetic mixes, which have no singing, MelBand RoFormer scored above DBS for the dub's voice split, so the dub default stays MelBand until real clips are rated blind. Steady hum goes mostly to music (BSRNN) or effects (TIGER); 20-31% of tape hiss stays in the dialogue. Split soundtrack's time estimate now uses the measured speeds (0.25x / 0.10x).
built: scripts/eval/metrics/fuobe_metrics/separation.py: SI-SDR and SDR per stem (a mono stem is scored against the reference's mono mean), whether the stems add up to the input, the bed's level and peak against the reference (catches AudioMerge's peak scaling), a stereo check (L/R correlation, width, per-channel level), where a known noise ends up, auto-alignment of the stems (AAC priming), WER on words, and speed from ComfyUI-DBS's report

Two new families in score.py and registry.py: 'separation' (voiceSiSdr, musicSiSdr, effectsSiSdr, backgroundSiSdr, voiceSdr, backgroundSdr, mixError, bedLevel, bedPeak, stereoCorrGap, noiseInVoice, speedX) and 'wer' (wer = the voice stem through Whisper base.en; werInput = the input as it is, i.e. without cleaning the voice first; werTranscript = the job's own Qwen3-ASR transcript). Whisper base.en is pinned at revision 911407f4 (MIT; the HF card says Apache-2.0). It is optional: requirements-asr.in/.txt (transformers 5.22.1), installed with pnpm eval:setup --asr

The runner records each output's stem name and the role of text outputs. The report shows one named audio player per stem. The blind review compares dialogue with dialogue and music & effects with music & effects as separate questions, with audio players, and serves audio file types

scripts/eval/fixtures/make-separation.py: builds 12 s 44.1 kHz stereo test mixes with known stems into local/separation/: centre, off-centre (panned left), 50 Hz hum, tape hiss, a loud master at -0.1 dBFS, and the centre mix inside an H.264+AAC video. Each mix gets a meta.json with the words, the levels and every source's licence. Music, effects, hum and hiss are synthesized from fixed seeds (CC0)

scripts/eval/cases/separation.json is generated by gen-cases.mjs; the DBS licences are read from the research JSON. Variants: bsrnn-mono, bsrnn-stereo, tiger-mono, tiger-stereo, dbs-dub (oss-dbs-voice-separate), melband (oss-voice-separate), demucs (cloud). A 'real' case takes your own clip for the blind A/B. A 'decides' rule is attached. SAM Audio is left out because samAudioCloud is false

Is D5 covered by this brief? Rule 14 says to include D5 if the brief covers it. The brief doesn't name D5, but it asks for §11's 'where does noise go', which the base's §11 says 'matters for Clean up dialogue'. It also asks for bed level against the reference and for WER of the cleaned voice, and those metrics measure D5's output directly. D5's open route is the ModelDef oss-dbs-remix (op separate-audio, graph soundtrack-remix-dbs, controls separationModel and channels, plus a bed level), so the suite's existing open target can run it. Its cloud cleaners (veed-clean-audio, deepfilternet3, ElevenLabs isolation) fit dry-run cloud variants, like demucs.

In §11, keep both measurements and say how they differ (D5: one mono Mandarin clip through graph C; D4: six stereo English mixes, by projection share). findings.title: `pnpm eval:setup --asr --download` fails: fuobe_metrics.download has no --asr flag
findings.detail: eval.mjs now adds `--asr` to the download step when both flags are given, and the HELP line advertises `[--asr] [--download ...]`, but download.py's argparse only knows --identity, --scrfd, --no-aesthetic and --dinov2. findings.title: The 'loud' fixture never triggers AudioMerge's peak scaling, so the check §2.1 hands to D4 is still unanswered
findings.detail: Research §2.1 says AudioMerge divides the fast stereo bed by its peak when it goes over 1.0, and that '§9 D4 checks it'. The brief asks for the bed's level and peak 'to catch AudioMerge's peak scaling'. The 'loud' mix normalises the whole mix to −0.1 dBFS with the music at −18 dBFS RMS, so the bed (mix − voice) peaks at about −7 dBFS on every run (bedPeak −7.0 to −7.3). The scaling path is never reached, and the doc can only say 'not triggered'. The metric is unit-tested, but the fixture doesn't exercise it.
findings.fix: Add or change a mix so the bed itself peaks at about −0.1 dBFS: music and effects dominant, loud transients, or the master normalised on the bed's peak. Rerun bsrnn-mono on it (about 50 s on the CPU ComfyUI) and record bedLevel and bedPeak in §9 D4.

findings.title: The blind review gives the model away by file extension on the dub comparison (DBS .flac against MelBand .mp3)

The DBS-vs-MelBand dub split is the one comparison the doc asks the owner to settle by rating real clips blind. This is new with audio pairs: the image and video suites rarely mix formats this way.

findings.title: Without the optional ASR install, the wer family drops werTranscript too, though it needs no ASR
findings.detail: m_wer computes werTranscript (the job's own Qwen3-ASR text against the known words), then calls self.asr(), which raises Missing when transformers isn't installed. The main loop catches Missing, drops the family's result, and marks 'wer' skipped for every later job. So the dub comparison loses its Qwen3 transcript WER unless `--asr` is installed, even though that score needs no model.
findings.fix: Call self.asr() only when there's a voice stem or input to transcribe, and catch Missing inside m_wer so werTranscript is kept, with a _note.
findings.verified: traced: m_wer → self.asr() → Asr.__init__ raises Missing → main loop `except Missing: scorer.skipped[fam]...; continue` (res discarded)

findings.title: The speech licence defaults to LibriSpeech whatever speech is given, and the case file doesn't record it
findings.detail: The brief asks for 'the licence of every fixture source in the case files'. The suite only points to each mix's meta.json, which is git-ignored and written locally. The speech's licence there comes from --speech-licence, which defaults to the LibriSpeech CC BY 4.0 string. A rerun with Fuobe TTS lines, the source the script's own docstring intends, records the wrong licence unless the user remembers to override it.
findings.fix: Make --speech-licence required, or read it from the speech folder (index.json or a licence.txt). Name the speech source of the measured runs (LibriSpeech dev-clean, CC BY 4.0) in the generated suite description next to the synthesized sources' CC0.

fix.finalSummary: DBS D4 is merged with the base that includes D5, and all eight review findings are fixed. The separation suite now covers Clean up dialogue on both engines. Open engine (your ComfyUI, CPU or GPU): DBS-BSRNN and DBS-TIGER, mono and each channel, the dub's DBS and MelBand voice splits, and Clean up dialogue through graph C. All of these were measured for real on this host's CPU ComfyUI. TIGER and the CUDA defaults still need a GPU. Cloud engine: Demucs and the D5 cleaners (VEED Clean Audio, DeepFilterNet 3) are built and tested as dry runs only. They need a fal key and a budget to measure; no paid call was made. SAM Audio is still absent (samAudioCloud false). New results: a loud master whose music reaches full scale does not trigger AudioMerge's peak scaling, because the bed went only to −0.07 dBFS (bedScale 0.00). Clean up dialogue's '−18 dB' preset actually leaves the music and effects at about −12.6 dB in the file, because DBS's dialogue stem already leaks the bed at about −18 dB. I recorded that in §9 D4 for the owner to judge by ear and did not change the preset. No defaults changed; DBS_SPEED stays 0.25x / 0.10x. Public sign-up is not affected: this package adds no routes, pages, graphs, ModelDefs or node packs. Its changes are evaluation tooling and docs. Guests and accounts get exactly what the base gives them for Split soundtrack and Clean up dialogue, including D5's own-GPU and own-files rules.
left: Clean up dialogue's bed comes out at about −12.6 dB with the −18 dB preset, because the dialogue stem leaks the bed at about −18 dB. Whether to lower the presets or change their labels is the owner's call after listening. The −14.5 dB figure for a −24 dB preset in the doc is arithmetic, not measured.
AudioMerge's scaling on an input that is itself over full scale was not measured: a float WAV, or an AAC decode of a loud master that overshoots.
The D5 speed gap (0.36–0.42x in D5's runs against 0.23–0.29x here, same graph and host) is unexplained. It is not the graph, the clip length or the sample rate.
The cloud cleaners and Demucs are dry runs only: no key and no paid call.
